artifacts.title: Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised.

artifacts.title: Application of BCO 24-1 examination process to re-election of officers

matches.evidence: BCO 24-1 applies fully to men with no prior official relationship to the church; for men already serving, lower courts determine which provisions apply at re-election.
